correctness.rationale: The all-delegating event has probability r^n and contributes zero correct ballots, zero caster weight, and a lost strict majority; it is kept explicitly. For k≥1 casters, clockwise positive run lengths are a composition of n; marking a starting caster gives multiplicity n/k per ordered k-composition. Independent caster correctness signs give the stated exact coefficient-extraction PGF. For the dispersion, ∑W_j² counts ordered pairs whose ballots terminate at the same caster. For two distinct voters at clockwise distance d, the common-caster probability is r^d+r^(n-d)-2r^n; diagonal entries contribute 1-r^n. Summing yields the exact Q formula. With fixed 0<q<1, a union bound on runs length L=ceil(4 log n/|log r|) gives max W=O_P(log n). Truncated local squared weights have dependency range O(log n) and Var(n^-1 sum)=O(log^5 n/n); their mean tends to (2-q)/q. The conditional centered weighted-sign array therefore satisfies Lindeberg, giving S_n/√n⇒N(2c_D,(2-q)/q). The direct indicators average to independent Bernoulli with mean 1/2+(qc_D+(1-q)c_A)/√n, giving a second binomial CLT. Strict normal CDF monotonicity yields the frontier, including exact no-claim on its equality line. Independent rational brute enumeration of all indicator and caster-signal realizations for q,p=(1/2,1/2),(2/5,3/5),(3/4,5/7) and n=2..9 confirms 24 PGF and exact Q instances; asymptotics rely on the proven probabilistic estimates, not these finite checks.

value.rationale: The cyclic delegation network is a minimal analytically tractable locality-constrained social-choice system. Its exact generating function and E∑W² measure how repeated ballots reuse the same noisy expert, and the limit derives a sharp, nontrivial information-versus-concentration competence threshold. The comparison can reverse depending on relative caster/noncaster skill, with the critical competence ratio explicit at q=1/2; the exact model boundary is mathematically motivated, not an arbitrary numerical example.

final_claim: On a fixed clockwise directed n-cycle with independent Bernoulli-q direct casters and transitive delegation, the correct-weight ballot PGF is r^n+∑_{k=1}^n (n/k)q^k r^(n-k)[t^n]((1-p)t/(1-t)+ptz/(1-tz))^k, with r=1-q; the exact weight dispersion is E∑W_j²=n[(2-q)/q-(2n-1+2/q)r^n]. Under local caster/noncaster accuracies 1/2+c_D/√n and 1/2+c_A/√n, c_D≥c_A≥0, the limiting delegated and direct strict-majority correctness probabilities are respectively Φ(2c_D√(q/(2-q))) and Φ(2(qc_D+(1-q)c_A)); delegation wins strictly in the limit iff c_D(√(q/(2-q))-q)>(1-q)c_A.
limitations: Applies only to independent casters on a one-way directed cycle, independent competence signals and fixed 0<q<1 local alternatives. No conclusions for correlated signals, other topologies, q varying with n, or exact equal-frontier finite ordering.
